priced_in_summary: Not a data-center-thesis call; a generic valuation-and-leverage-overshoot call that happens to sit on this chain's link, the same shape as AECOM's INVESTABLE call on this identical link. The method's TOO_LATE test asks whether the decomposition shows multiple expansion eating the runway, and here it shows the extreme opposite: trailing P/E fell from roughly 55.8x to roughly 25.2x over the past year even as FY2025 net income grew 41.52%, driven not by a miss but by a real, disclosed, dated balance-sheet event (closing the $3.3 billion, partly debt-funded TRC acquisition, which pushed leverage to 2.3x against a 1.0x-2.0x target) landing in the same window as three consecutive guidance raises, a record backlog and accelerating organic growth. What the price asks for, on this dive's own corrected-leverage reverse-DCF read (deliberately harder than the filed, stale-net-debt convention, which is if anything friendlier to this thesis and not relied on), is only about 1.0% real free-cash-flow growth in perpetuity. This dive's own bear-case rebuild (4.0% FCF-CAGR-equivalent, built from nothing but the LOW END of WSP's own guided FY2026 organic growth range, no margin credit, no M&A credit) already clears that ask by roughly 3 percentage points, comfortably outside the filed solve's own 1.4-point horizon-spread tolerance, and the base case (8.08%) clears it by roughly 7 points. Set against that: this is the third O1 dive on a link with zero company-specific revenue attribution, the elevated leverage and share-count dilution are real and current rather than merely historical, and the TRC integration itself is unproven (no combined fiscal year of results exists yet). The honest verdict is INVESTABLE: a real, disclosed, bounded overshoot with a margin of safety that survives this dive's own deliberately harder-than-filed bear case, priced by a market that has just watched this name close a large debt-funded acquisition and may still be right to demand proof the leverage normalizes on the guided timeline, which is exactly what no_entry_above and the independence test's falsification condition are for.

FAVORABLE (undervalued), and robust even under a deliberately harder-than-filed convention. Building FY2030 FCF from this dive's own revenue, margin and cash-conversion rows (base case: 7% revenue CAGR to $25.65 billion, 10.2% operating margin giving $2.616 billion operating income, FY2025's own operating-income-to-FCF conversion ratio of 1.1803x applied, giving $3.087 billion FCF against a $2.093 billion base) gives a base-case FCF-CAGR-equivalent of 8.08%, and a bear case (4% revenue CAGR, flat 9.70% margin, flat 1.1803x conversion) gives 4.00%. Forward-evaluating quality.reverse_dcf's own bisection formula (replicated to reproduce the filed enterprise values to within 0.02% before varying inputs) against a market-implied ask that this dive corrects for WSP's own disclosed post-TRC-close leverage (net debt approximately $6.67 billion rather than the filed, stale $3.30 billion) gives an implied ask at today's actual price of +1.03%, a gap of 7.05 percentage points for the base case and 2.97 points for the bear case, both well outside the filed solve's own 1.4-point horizon_spread: a real gap, not a horizon artifact, even on the harder convention. On the filed, uncorrected net-debt convention the gap is even wider (base case gap 8.94 points against a -0.86% ask at the filed price, or 9.66 points against this dive's own -1.58% replication at today's actual close), which this dive deliberately does not rely on because it rests on a stale balance-sheet snapshot that predates a real, disclosed leverage increase. Converting each case to a price via the corrected-net-debt bisection formula: bear $211.71, base $260.95, bull $332.45, all above today's $180.17 close.

independence_test.largest_disagreement: The market is pricing WSP's forward free cash flow at close to flat in perpetuity: even after correcting the filed reverse-DCF's stale, pre-TRC-close net-debt input for WSP's own disclosed current leverage (2.3x as of 2026-06-26), today's actual close implies roughly +1.0% real FCF growth forever (versus an even more negative -1.6% on the filed, stale-debt convention, which is if anything friendlier to this thesis and deliberately not relied on), while even a bear-case rebuild using only the low end of WSP's own guided 4%-7% FY2026 organic growth range, no further margin expansion, and no credit for continued bolt-on M&A, already implies about 4.0% FCF-CAGR-equivalent growth, roughly 3 percentage points above what the market is asking, comfortably outside the filed solve's own 1.4-point horizon-spread tolerance.
independence_test.why_the_gap_exists: Recency bias around one real, disclosed, already-guided-to-normalize balance-sheet event. Closing the $3.3 billion, largely debt-funded TRC acquisition pushed WSP's leverage to 2.3x as of 2026-06-26, above management's own 1.0x-2.0x target range, and diluted shares outstanding (Piotroski's own share-count criterion fails for FY2025, and the FY2026 count is very likely higher still). The market appears to be extrapolating that one-time, disclosed, already-guided-to-be-temporary leverage and dilution event onto WSP's whole steady-state cash-generation capacity, even as the same quarter's own results showed record backlog (+23.2% year over year to $20.1 billion), accelerating organic growth (5.0% in Q2 2026, the high end of guidance) and a record Q2 EBITDA margin, none of which the filed reverse-DCF's stale, FY2025-year-end-based net-debt input can see. This valuation disagreement does not depend on the data-center-moratoria occurrence at all: the gap-table build above rests entirely on company-wide backlog, margin and leverage figures, none of them data-center-specific, consistent with priced_in_summary.
independence_test.falsification: Stated to prove this dive WRONG, not to confirm it. At WSP's Q3 FY2026 results (expected around early-to-mid November 2026, inside review_by), if leverage has NOT moved back toward management's own guided sub-2.0x target and/or organic net revenue growth has fallen below the low end of the guided 4%-7% FY2026 range, that would show the market was right to price the TRC-related balance-sheet event as a lasting impairment of cash-generation capacity rather than a temporary, already-guided-to-normalize one, and this dive would be wrong. A single-legged test deliberately: an in-line outcome (leverage trending down, organic growth staying inside guidance) tests the dive rather than confirming it by construction.

earnings_quality.basis: Every mechanically computable input from the four-part veto battery is clean or unremarkable, but two real, disclosed, recent balance-sheet events (both already guided by management to normalize) keep this off a clean A. Accruals: -3.92% of average total assets in FY2024 and -6.25% in FY2025, both well inside the 5% caution band and strongly in the conservative direction (operating cash flow exceeded net income by 700.5 million and 1,281.7 million CAD respectively). Beneish M-score -2.828 against the -1.78 review threshold, CLEAN, 12 of 12 inputs found. DSO improved over the most recent year (68.29, 59.75, 65.78, 51.89 days FY2022-FY2025), not the sustained multi-year drift method section 7 flags. Capex to depreciation is low and asset-light throughout (0.289, 0.268, 0.239, 0.204 FY2022-FY2025), consistent with a professional-services business, though the ratio's steady decline is named plainly as a mild watch item rather than a capex holiday (no single-year cliff). Piotroski is 7 of 9, STRONG, missing d_leverage's sibling shares criterion and asset_turnover, both plausibly explained by the same TRC acquisition (dilutive share issuance, acquired-goodwill-heavy asset base) that this dive already treats as the central, temporary risk. TWO REAL FLAGS, both disclosed rather than hidden and both already guided by management to normalize, are why this is B and not A: (1) leverage of 2.3x as of 2026-06-26, above WSP's own 1.0x-2.0x target range, disclosed in the same 2026-08-05 release that raised guidance, with management's own stated expectation to return to the target range by year end 2026; (2) share count rose 3.32% FY2024 to FY2025 (130,479,453 to 134,806,772) and the TRC deal (partly funded via debt and, per WSP's own disclosure, an equity component) almost certainly diluted further in 2026, not yet reflected in this vendor block's FY2025-year-end figures. Neither flag is Beneish-breach- or channel-stuffing-shaped (no mechanical input above points to manipulation), which is why this does not reach grade C, but two real, disclosed, current balance-sheet events landing in the same quarter as the largest acquisition in the company's recent history is more than 'no flags', hence B. No deferred-revenue or contract-liability series exists in the vendor block for this issuer and no primary filing exists to recover one (WSP carries no SEC CIK), so this leg of the veto battery rests on the DSO reading alone rather than a second corroborating series, named plainly in data_gaps rather than smoothed over.

earnings_quality.veto_applied: Grade B has no cap effect (method section 7): only C, D, or an uncomputable grade change what this verdict may be. pre_mortem.instruction: Twelve months from now this INVESTABLE call was wrong. Three most likely reasons, and whether the market would have been right.
reasons: TRC integration underperforms the guide: cost overruns, client attrition, or a goodwill impairment on the newly acquired Power and Energy business keep leverage above the 1.0x-2.0x target well past year-end 2026, and the market correctly priced the debt-funded acquisition as a lasting impairment of cash-generation capacity rather than the temporary, already-guided-to-normalize event this dive assumed. This is exactly what the independence test's falsification condition is built to catch, at the Q3 FY2026 release inside review_by.

A sector-wide, not WSP-specific, re-rating continues or deepens: the same window that hit AECOM alongside WSP suggests a systematic repricing of engineering and environmental-consulting peer multiples (higher required discount rates, lower peer multiples industry-wide, e.g. from an infrastructure-capex slowdown or a rate-environment shift), which a single-company reverse-DCF correction cannot defend against even if WSP's own fundamentals hold up exactly as guided. Here the market would not be wrong about WSP specifically so much as right that the whole peer group re-rates, and this dive's 9% discount-rate assumption (inherited unchanged from the filed convention) turns out too low for the environment twelve months out.

Working-capital drag from integrating a large, newly acquired, lower-margin business erodes the FY2025 cash-conversion ratio (1.1803x operating-income-to-FCF) this dive holds flat in its own bear case; if FCF conversion falls materially below that level for several quarters while TRC integrates, the bear case's own 4.00% FCF-CAGR-equivalent floor overstates realized cash generation, and the market was right to discount the reported backlog and organic-growth figures more heavily than the guided-low-end assumption credits.
pre_mortem.downgrade_trigger: Not triggered: all three reasons are ones under which the market's caution would have been the correct call, not merely ones where the analyst got unlucky. No automatic downgrade to WATCH.
